req.title: Show index page
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

doc.reasoning: The test suite is designed to validate the functionality of the index page of the blogging application. It ensures that the page correctly lists all posts in descending order of creation, handles errors appropriately, and respects boundary conditions.

tests.name: test_index_page_positive
preconditions: Database is initialized with pre-loaded data.
actions: Send a GET request to the '/' endpoint.
expected: HTML page with post titles in descending order of creation.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Initialize the database
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data  # Most recent post
assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r.data  # Oldest post

tests.name: test_index_page_negative
preconditions: Database is initialized with pre-loaded data.
actions: Simulate a server error by tampering with the database connection.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Simulate a server error by closing the database connection
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import close_db
    close_db()

try:
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code >= 500
except Exception as e:
    assert isinstance(e, Exception)

tests.name: test_index_page_boundary
preconditions: Database is initialized with pre-loaded data.
actions: Send a GET request to the '/' endpoint with a large number of posts.
expected: HTML page with all post titles in descending order of creation.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Initialize the database
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    # Insert boundary-valid posts
    for i in range(21, 41):
        db.execute('INSERT INTO post (id, author_id, created, title, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)', (i, 1, '2025-04-01 10:30:37', 'Boundary Post ' + str(i), 'Content'))
    db.commit()

r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'Boundary Post 40' in r.data
assert b'Boundary Post 21' in r.data
